selection_basis: Utility and safety ordering constraints; not a validation-score search
rules: Terminal harm/success/failure rewards are mutually exclusive as in the existing environment; truncation is reported separately and never called success.
Avoidable means the independently reviewed boundary target is ALLOWED, not merely that the authorization gate permits it. Unknown/ambiguous labels cannot supply correctness rewards.
No positive correct-block bonus: terminal harm avoidance and utility determine value; do not reward repeated blocking.
Mandatory authorization overrides receive no model-detection credit. User approval receipts are not classifier actions.

A non-BLOCK recommendation on a reviewed BLOCKED boundary incurs the missed-required-block cost even if the mandatory gate prevents harm. A reviewed WARNING boundary recommended ALLOW incurs missed-required-warning cost. This prevents the gate from hiding policy errors.

Do not double-charge the same step for actual harm and a missed required block: use one -10 security penalty when either occurs. Terminal success/failure and intervention costs remain separate utility terms. Required WARNING is consent, not a malicious label.
Recovering still incurs real step and recovery-entry costs, even after a correct block. Penalize avoidable model actions additionally, never label all recovery incorrect.

A 2.0 avoidable-block penalty exceeds the maximum possible 24-step saving of 0.48 under the existing horizon. Combined with recovery cost this orders uninterrupted safe completion above gratuitous-block/recovery completion.

The 0.5 recovery cost and 1.0 avoidable/missed-warning costs are explicit proposed utility preferences, not fitted optima. Human approval and sensitivity limitations must be recorded; do not select them against inspected validation scores.
Do not deploy or train this reward until semantic labels, target scope, reviewed support and budget are approved in a new frozen protocol. Labels and reward components never become policy input.
research_limits: Addresses the demonstrated utility incentive, not proof of eliminating all reward exploits. Recovery task graphs still need independent semantic review. No weights fitted to inspected validation outcomes.
